chunks: And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Ibn Hakim, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) or his father (peace be upon him) (1), that he said:

Regarding the divorced woman whose husband divorces her, and she says, 'I am pregnant,' and she remains for a year, he said: 'If she brings him forth for more than a year, she is not verified, even if it is by one hour.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a divorced woman's claim of pregnancy if she gives birth after one year?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Tahdhib clarifies the evidentiary standard for a divorced woman claiming pregnancy to extend her 'iddah, establishing that a full year of residence serves as a presumptive proof unless she delivers within that period. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the burden of proof lies on the claimant if delivery occurs within the year, ensuring financial and legal clarity regarding paternity and maintenance.
